## ALPHA DIVERSITY

```{r cars}
#ALPHA DIVERSITY##############################################################

# Transpose the data so that columns become rows (samples)
data <- read.csv('votus_dataset2_TMM_rel_abund.txt', sep = '\t', row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

# Ensure all data are numeric
data <- as.data.frame(lapply(data, as.numeric), row.names = rownames(data))

# Apply log(x + 1) transformation
data_log <- log1p(data) 

data_transposed <- t(data_log)

# Check if data is numeric and properly formatted
str(data_transposed)
data_transposed <- as.matrix(data_transposed)
head(data_transposed)
```

## Calculate alpha diversity indexes 

```{r cars2}
# Shannon diversity index
shannon_diversity <- diversity(data_transposed, index = "shannon")
shannon_diversity

```
```{r cars3}
# Observed diversity index (Species Richness)
observed <- specnumber(data_transposed)
observed


```
```{r cars3}
# Simpsom index
simpson_diversity <- diversity(data_transposed, index = "simpson")
simpson_diversity


```

## Prepare the table

```{r cars4}
# Combine the indices into a single data frame for plotting
diversity_data_per_sample <- data.frame(
  samples = c('AP1','AP1','AP1','AP2','AP2','AP2','AP3','AP3','AP3','AP4','AP4','AP4','AP5','AP5','AP5',
              'BP1','BP1','BP1','BP2','BP2','BP2','BP3','BP3','BP3','BP4','BP4','BP4','BP5','BP5','BP5',
             'MP1','MP1','MP1','MP2','MP2','MP2','MP3','MP3','MP3','MP4','MP4','MP4','MP5','MP5','MP5',
             'PP1','PP1','PP1','PP2','PP2','PP2','PP3','PP3','PP3','PP4','PP4','PP4','PP5','PP5','PP5'),
  Shannon = shannon_diversity,
  Observed = observed,
  Simpson = simpson_diversity
)
diversity_data_per_sample

# Saving the diversity data table
#write.table(diversity_data, 'diversity_data_table.tsv', sep = '\t', row.names = FALSE)
```
```{r cars4}
# Combine the indices into a single data frame for plotting
diversity_data_per_city <- data.frame(
  samples = c('Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira','Altamira',
              'Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca','Braganca',
             'Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba','Maraba',
             'Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas','Paragominas'),
  Shannon = shannon_diversity,
  Observed = observed,

)
```

# Normality of data evalation per sample

```{r cars5}
# Combine the indices into a single data frame for plotting
#Statistical tests: ANOVA ##################################
#Normalidade
byf.shapiro(Shannon ~ samples, diversity_data_per_sample) 
#byf.shapiro(Simpson ~ samples, diversity_data)
#byf.shapiro(Observed ~ samples, diversity_data_per_sample) 
byf.shapiro(Simpson ~ samples, diversity_data_per_sample) 
```
## ANOVA and bonferonni post-hoc for Shannon species index
```{r cars6}
anova_shannon <- aov(Shannon ~ samples, diversity_data_per_sample)
summary(anova_shannon)
  #post-hoc
PostHocTest(anova_shannon, method = "bonf")
```
## ANOVA and bonferonni post-hoc for observed species index
```{r cars7}
#ANOVA
anova_observed <- aov(Observed ~ samples, diversity_data_per_sample)
summary(anova_observed)
#post-hoc
PostHocTest(anova_observed, method = "bonf")
```
## Alpha diversity boxplots per sample

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
#Preparing the table for plooting##########################################

# Melt the data for easier plotting
diversity_data_melted <- melt(diversity_data_per_sample, id.vars = "samples")
diversity_data_melted
#write.table(diversity_data_melted, 'diversity_data_melt_table.tsv',sep='\t',row.names = FALSE)

# Generate separate box plots for each diversity index using facet_wrap
ggplot(diversity_data_melted, aes(x = samples, y = value, fill = variable)) +
geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Alpha Diversity Indices for Each Sample", x = "Sample", y = "Diversity Index Value") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +  # Separate facets for each index (Shannon, Simpson, Species Richness)
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for readability

```

# Plottig the alpha div graph but with different shapes depending on the city point
```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

set.seed(1234)

diversity_data_per_city$point <- c('P1','P1','P1','P2','P2','P2','P3','P3','P3','P4','P4','P4','P5','P5','P5',
                                   'P1','P1','P1','P2','P2','P2','P3','P3','P3','P4','P4','P4','P5','P5','P5',
                                   'P1','P1','P1','P2','P2','P2','P3','P3','P3','P4','P4','P4','P5','P5','P5',
                                   'P1','P1','P1','P2','P2','P2','P3','P3','P3','P4','P4','P4','P5','P5','P5')

# ---- Prepare table for plotting ----

# Only keep numeric diversity metrics + metadata
div_long <- melt(
  diversity_data_per_city[, c("samples", "Shannon", "Observed", "point")],
  id.vars = c("samples", "point")
)

# Ensure numeric
div_long$value <- as.numeric(as.character(div_long$value))

# Keep only the Shannon data for this plot
shannon_melted <- subset(div_long, variable == "Shannon")

# ---- Plot ----
p <- ggplot(shannon_melted, aes(x = samples, y = value, fill = samples)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = TRUE, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6, width = 0.6, coef = 0) +
  geom_jitter(aes(shape = point), color = "black", size = 4, width = 0.15, show.legend = TRUE) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Altamira" = "#E69F00",
    "Braganca" = "#56B4E9",
    "Maraba" = "#009E73",
    "Paragominas" = "#CC79A7"
  )) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(
    "P1" = 21, "P2" = 22, "P3" = 23, "P4" = 24, "P5" = 25
  )) +

  labs(title = "Shannon diversity value for each Sample",
       x = NULL, y = "Shannon Index Value",
       fill = "City", shape = "Collection point") +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    tag = 'A'
  )
   theme(plot.tag.position = c(0.01, 1), # Position the tag in the top-left corner of the entire figure
        plot.tag = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 50, face = "bold"))

# ---- Significance annotations ----
max_y <- max(shannon_melted$value, na.rm = TRUE)

p <- p +
  geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("Altamira", "Maraba")),
              annotations = "***",
              y_position = max_y * 1.05) +
  geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("Braganca", "Maraba")),
              annotations = "***",
              y_position = max_y * 1.07) +
  geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("Braganca", "Paragominas")),
              annotations = "*",
              y_position = max_y * 1.09) +
  geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("Paragominas", "Maraba")),
              annotations = "***",
              y_position = max_y * 1.12) + 
  guides(fill = "none")
p
tiff("viral_shannon_div_with_diff_shapes.tiff",  width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300)
print(p)
dev.off()

```

## BETA DIVERSITY

## PCoA per city
```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}
# PCoA per city
# Beta DIVERSITY with PCoA ##################################################
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)

# Replace NA with 0
data_transposed[is.na(data_transposed)] <- 0

# Bray-Curtis distances
bc_dist <- vegdist(data_transposed, method = "bray")

# Perform PCoA
pcoa_res <- cmdscale(bc_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2) # k = 2 axes

# Convert to dataframe for plotting
pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(pcoa_res$points),
  Axis1 = pcoa_res$points[,1],
  Axis2 = pcoa_res$points[,2]
)

# Criar coluna City com nomes completos
# Extract the first two letters of the sample name
pcoa_df$City <- substr(pcoa_df$Sample, 1, 2)

# Use ifelse to map the two-letter codes to full city names
pcoa_df$City <- ifelse(pcoa_df$City == "AP", "Altamira",
                       ifelse(pcoa_df$City == "BP", "Braganca",
                              ifelse(pcoa_df$City == "MP", "Maraba",
                                     ifelse(pcoa_df$City == "PP", "Paragominas", pcoa_df$City))))

# Variance explained
var_explained <- round(100 * pcoa_res$eig / sum(pcoa_res$eig), 2)

# Definir cores fixas para cada cidade
city_colors <- c("Altamira" = "#1f77b4",     # azul
                 "Braganca" = "#ff7f0e",     # laranja
                 "Maraba" = "#2ca02c",       # verde
                 "Paragominas" = "#d62728")  # vermelho

city_colors_enhanced <- c(
"Altamira" = "#E69F00",  
    "Braganca" = "#56B4E9",  
    "Maraba" = "#009E73",    
    "Paragominas" = "#CC79A7" 
)

p <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, fill = City)) +
   
  geom_point(shape = 21, color='black', size = 4, alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0.8) +
  
  
  # Set colors for the border (color) and fill (fill)
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = city_colors_enhanced, name = "City") +
  
  labs(
    title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis)",
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_explained[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_explained[2], "%)")
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    # Customize axis lines/ticks
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill=NA, linewidth=1),
    
    # Position the legend clearly
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # Clean up legend keys
    
    # Ensure axis labels are bold
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    
    # Remove plot title as requested in the initial code (you can add one if needed)
    plot.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    tag = 'B'
  )
   theme(plot.tag.position = c(0.01, 1), # Position the tag in the top-left corner of the entire figure
        plot.tag = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 50, face = "bold"))
p
# Show plot
tiff("viral_betadiv_PCoA.tiff", width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300)
print(p)
dev.off()

```

#Enviromental variables influence (with PCoA)
#Env fit
```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}
library(vegan)

# bc_dist must already exist (Bray–Curtis or other)
# Example: bc_dist <- vegdist(t(abund_table), method = "bray")

pcoa_res <- cmdscale(bc_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)  # 2 PCoA axes
pcoa_coords <- as.data.frame(pcoa_res$points)
colnames(pcoa_coords) <- c("PCoA1", "PCoA2")

# Make sure rownames match your sample order
pcoa_coords$SampleID <- rownames(pcoa_coords)

env_data <- read.csv("env_data.tsv.txt", sep = "\t")

# Ensure same sample order
env_data <- env_data[match(pcoa_coords$SampleID, env_data$SampleID), ]
rownames(env_data) <- env_data$SampleID

fit <- envfit(pcoa_coords[, c("PCoA1", "PCoA2")], 
              env_data, 
              permutations = 999)

fit
```
#Mantel
```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}

vars <- rownames(fit$vectors$arrows)

envfit_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = vars,
  R2 = fit$vectors$r,
  P = fit$vectors$pvals
)

envfit_sig <- subset(envfit_df, P < 0.05)

env_data_numeric <- env_data[, 2:8]   # modify as needed

mantel_results <- lapply(colnames(env_data_numeric), function(var) {
  
  x <- env_data_numeric[[var]]

  x_scaled <- scale(x)
  
  x_dist <- dist(x_scaled, method = "euclidean")
  
  m <- mantel(bc_dist, x_dist, method = "spear", permutations = 9999)
  
  data.frame(Variable = var, Mantel_r = m$statistic)
})

mantel_df <- bind_rows(mantel_results)

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

p1 <- ggplot(envfit_df, aes(x = R2, y = reorder(Variable, R2))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Goodness of fit (R²)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size= 15)
  )

p2 <- ggplot(mantel_df, aes(x = Mantel_r, y = reorder(Variable, Mantel_r))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "yellow") +
  labs(title = "Mantel statistic (r)", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size= 15)
  )

tiff("envfit_vs_mantel.tiff", width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2) 
dev.off()


```

#NMDS per city
```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}

# NMDS with Bray-Curtis #####################################################
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)

# Replace NA with 0
data_transposed[is.na(data_transposed)] <- 0  

# Bray-Curtis distances
bc_dist <- vegdist(data_transposed, method = "bray")

# Run NMDS (k=2 for 2D ordination)
nmds_res <- metaMDS(bc_dist, k = 2, trymax = 100)

# Extract site scores (samples in reduced space)
nmds_points <- as.data.frame(scores(nmds_res, display = "sites"))
nmds_points$Sample <- rownames(nmds_points)

# Extract City name
nmds_points$City <- sub("^([A-Z]{2}).*$", "\\1", nmds_points$Sample)

lookup <- c("AP" = "Altamira",
            "BP" = "Braganca",
            "MP" = "Maraba",
            "PP" = "Paragominas")

nmds_points$City <- lookup[nmds_points$City]

# Definir cores fixas
```

``` {r pressure2, echo=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
# Make sure to load 'dplyr' if you haven't, for piping and data manipulation

# 1. Define Professional Color Palette for Cities
# Using colors that are distinct and aesthetically pleasing (e.g., from ColorBrewer)

  # Use shape 21 (circle with border) for better visual quality
  geom_point(shape = 21, color='black', size = 4, alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0.8) +
  
  # Set colors for the border (color) and fill (fill)

  scale_fill_manual(values = city_colors_enhanced, name = "City") +
  
  # Add Axes Labels
  labs(
    x = "NMDS1",
    y = "NMDS2"
  ) +
  
  # Use a clean, publication-ready theme
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    # Customize axis lines/ticks
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill=NA, linewidth=1),
    
    # Position the legend clearly
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA), # Clean up legend keys
    
    # Ensure axis labels are bold
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    
    # Remove plot title as requested in the initial code (you can add one if needed)
    plot.title = element_blank()
  ) +
  
  # 4. Add Annotations (Stress and K value, similar to the image's format)
  annotate("text",
           x = max(nmds_points$NMDS1, na.rm = TRUE), # Position at bottom right
           y = min(nmds_points$NMDS2, na.rm = TRUE),
           label = paste("K =", 2, "  Stress =", stress_value),
           hjust = 1.0, vjust = 0, size = 4, fontface = "bold")
```

```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}
#Calculate manntel statistics
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(gridExtra)


env_data <- env_data[,2:10]
mantel_results <- lapply(colnames(env_data), function(var) {
  
  # get 1 column only
  x <- env_data[[var]]
  
  # scale variable
  x_scaled <- scale(x)
  
  # euclidean distance
  x_dist <- dist(x_scaled, method = "euclidean")
  
  # mantel test vs Bray–Curtis
  m <- mantel(bc_dist, x_dist, method = "spear", permutations = 9999)
  
  data.frame(Variable = var, Mantel_r = m$statistic)
})

mantel_df <- bind_rows(mantel_results)

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

p1 <- ggplot(envfit_df, aes(x = R2, y = reorder(Variable, R2))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "purple") +
  labs(title = "Goodness of fit  r²", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

p2 <- ggplot(mantel_df, aes(x = Mantel_r, y = reorder(Variable, Mantel_r))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "yellow") +
  labs(title = "Mantel statistic  r", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

```{r pressure2, echo=FALSE}

library(vegan)

# Ensure City is a factor
nmds_points$City <- as.factor(nmds_points$City)

# Get all unique city combinations
city_pairs <- combn(levels(nmds_points$City), 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Empty list to store results
anosim_pairs <- list()

for (pair in city_pairs) {
  
  # Get sample names belonging to both cities in the pair
  subset_samples <- nmds_points$SampleID[nmds_points$City %in% pair]
  
  # Subset the distance matrix by sample names to avoid indexing errors
  subset_dist <- bc_dist[subset_samples, subset_samples]
  subset_dist <- as.dist(subset_dist)   # convert back to 'dist'
  
  # Subset grouping factor
  subset_group <- factor(nmds_points$City[nmds_points$SampleID %in% subset_samples])
  
  # Run ANOSIM
  res <- anosim(subset_dist, grouping = subset_group, permutations = 999)
  
  # Store result
  key <- paste(pair, collapse = "_vs_")
  anosim_pairs[[key]] <- c(R = res$statistic, P = res$signif)
}

anosim_pairs
```

```{r cars9}

# Load required package
library(vegan)

# 1. Load your data ----
# comm = community abundance table (samples x taxa), rownames = sample IDs
# meta = metadata with at least a column "Site" for Altamira, Braganca, etc.

comm <- read.table("community_table.tsv", header=TRUE, row.names=1, sep="\t")
meta <- read.table("metadata.tsv", header=TRUE, sep="\t", row.names=1)

# Ensure sample order matches
comm <- comm[rownames(meta), ]

# 2. Calculate Bray-Curtis distance ----
bray_dist <- vegdist(comm, method="bray")

# 3. PERMANOVA ----
# Tests whether communities differ by site
perm <- adonis2(bray_dist ~ Site, data=meta, permutations=999)
print(perm)

# 4. Test homogeneity of dispersion (betadisper) ----
bd <- betadisper(bray_dist, meta$Site)
anova(bd)              # test significance
permutest(bd)          # permutation test
plot(bd)               # visualize group dispersions

# 5. NMDS ----
nmds <- metaMDS(comm, distance="bray", k=2, trymax=100)
plot(nmds, type="n")
points(nmds, display="sites", col=as.factor(meta$Site), pch=19)

# 6. Fit environmental variables (if you have them) ----
# Example: meta has columns pH, TDS, DO, etc.
env <- meta[, c("pH", "TDS", "DO")]   # adjust to your variables
fit <- envfit(nmds, env, permutations=999)
print(fit)
plot(fit, p.max=0.05, col="black")   # plot only significant vectors


```
